messages.subject: Re: brain registration
messages.body_plain:
Dear Emilia,

Unfortunately the Stanford server died and couldn't be replaced at that address. The new location for information / downloads for the registration tools is:

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=warping_manual:start

We actually now recommend saving input images in nrrd format according to the instructions at

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=warping_manual:registration_gui

The relevant plugins are bundled with Fiji by default and can be accessed by File ... Save as ... Nrrd

Incidentally if you look at the bottom of the page you will see a download for the classic macosx gui, although we now recommend the CMTK registration plugin that you have already installed.

Best wishes,

Greg Jefferis.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing this message to the nat-user google group since the answer may be of interest to others.

On 21 Jun 2018, at 12:44, Moscato, Emilia wrote:
>
> Hi Dr. Jefferis,
> I am a post-doc in Matthew Kayser's lab at the University of Pennsylvania. We are trying to register brain images so that we can identify neurons of interest within a broad driver. I installed the CMTK registration plug-in in FIJI, but I am having trouble finding the Biorad Writer and Nrrd Reader plug-in and the IGS registration tools mentioned in your 2013 CSH protocol (Ostrovsky, Cachero, Jefferis) and the registration GUI read-me. In the CSH protocol, the link to the plug-ins no longer work (http://flybrain.stanford.edu/imageJplugins). Are these still publicly available, in a different place?
> Thanks for your help,
> Emilia Moscato

--
Gregory Jefferis, PhD
Division of Neurobiology
MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
Francis Crick Avenue
Cambridge Biomedical Campus
Cambridge, CB2 OQH, UK
